findings.issue: KMS key policy lockout safety check can be disabled
findings.risk: Setting bypass_policy_lockout_safety_check to true can allow creation of a key policy that removes administrative access to the key, causing loss of control over the key or unsafe policy deployment.
findings.remediation: Set the aws_kms_key.this attribute bypass_policy_lockout_safety_check = false, or remove the attribute so the safety check remains enforced.

findings.issue: Overly permissive default key policy grants kms:* to the account root principal
findings.risk: Granting full KMS administration and usage permissions with actions = ["kms:*"] to the account root principal enables broad privilege escalation and unrestricted use or management of the key by any IAM principal that can obtain delegated access.
findings.remediation: Disable the broad default statement by setting var.enable_default_policy = false, or replace the statement sid = "Default" with least-privilege actions such as administrative actions only and separate narrowly scoped usage statements.

findings.issue: Overly permissive key owner policy grants kms:* to all configured key owners
findings.risk: Granting actions = ["kms:*"] to all principals in var.key_owners gives unrestricted administrative and cryptographic access, increasing the blast radius of credential compromise and violating least privilege.
findings.remediation: Modify the statement sid = "KeyOwner" in data.aws_iam_policy_document.this to replace actions = ["kms:*"] with a minimal set of required administrative or usage actions, or move broad permissions into separate tightly scoped statements for specific principals.
